home.title: Big Cube Solver - every cube from 2×2 to 15×15
home.lead: Point your phone's camera at any cube from 2×2 to 15×15 and follow a short solution, move by move, on a 3D cube - with the real one in your hands.
home.soon: Android · coming soon to Google Play
home.what.sub: Most solvers stop at 6×6 or 7×7. This one keeps going to 15×15 - and it runs on modest phones too, from Android 5.0 up.
home.f1.d: Custom solvers reduce a 15×15 to a 13×13, then 11×11 ... down to a 3×3, so you never wade through thousands of needless moves.
home.f2.d: Animated 3D moves you can step, rewind, slow down or speed up, in chapters: centres, edges, the final 3×3.
home.f3.d: Turned centres are solved too, so every photo or logo comes back whole and upright.
home.f4.d: Show each face and the colours are read automatically - odd colour schemes are read as they are.
home.f5.d: Spirals, rings, checkerboards, cubes in cubes on every size - and your own, shared as a link.
home.f6.d: Draw on a face or place stickers one by one, and the app finds the moves.
home.turns.sub: Average turns to solve a random cube with the short solver. A regular solver answers in seconds on any phone, with more moves - choose per size.

faq.title: Q&A - Big Cube Solver
faq.cubes:
Which cubes does it solve?

Every standard cube from 2×2 to 15×15, plus 3×3 picture cubes, where the centres must also face the right way.
faq.phones:
Which phones does it run on?

Android 5.0 or newer. It was built to run on modest phones too: even a 15×15 solves on an old phone with 1 GB of memory.
faq.iphone:
Is there an iPhone version?

Not for now - Big Cube Solver is Android only.
faq.when:
When will it be on Google Play?

Soon. It is in testing now. You can try it before everyone else: become a tester.
faq.price:
How much does it cost?

2×2, 3×3 and 4×4 are free, forever. The bigger sizes are one-time purchases: up to 10×10, or up to 15×15 with picture cubes and smart cubes. No subscription and no ads; the prices will be shown in Google Play.
faq.data:
Does it need the internet? Does it collect data?

No and no. Scanning and solving happen on the phone, the app has no account, ads or tracking, and nothing leaves your phone. Details in the privacy policy.
faq.moves:
How many moves are the solutions?

About 19 turns for a 3×3, 43 for a 4×4, 69 for a 5×5, 200 for a 7×7, 620 for a 10×10 and 1,750 for a 15×15, on average.
faq.why15:
Why does a 15×15 need so many moves?

A 15×15 has 1,014 centre pieces and 156 edge pieces to bring home - a 3×3 has none of the first kind. The app reduces the cube step by step (15×15 to 13×13, to 11×11 ... to 3×3) to keep the count as low as it can.
faq.short:
Short or regular solver - which should I use?

The short solver finds far fewer moves; the regular one answers in seconds on any phone. The first time you open the app the short solvers get ready in the background (about a minute, longer on older phones). You can choose per size.
faq.notation:
Which notation does it use?

Standard (WCA) notation: R, U', F2, wide turns such as 3Rw, and x, y, z for turning the whole cube. Every move is also animated on the 3D cube, so you never need to read it.
faq.tips:
Tips for scanning my cube

Use even light without glare or strong shadows, hold each face straight and let it fill the guide. Cubes with unusual colours are read as they are. If a sticker is read wrong, correct it before solving.
faq.smart:
Which smart cubes work?

Several Bluetooth smart cubes, including Giiker, GAN and QiYi models: the screen follows every turn you make. If yours does not connect, tell us its brand and model at support.
faq.location:
Why does it ask for location with Bluetooth?

On Android 6 to 11, Android itself requires the location permission to look for Bluetooth devices. The app never reads your location.
faq.share:
How do I share a pattern?

In the app, long-press a pattern in My patterns and choose Share: it becomes a link. Whoever opens it on an Android phone with the app gets it in their My patterns. More in Patterns.
faq.more: Not answered here? Write to support.

sup.intro: Something not working, a question, an idea? Write to us. We read every message.

sup.inc.h: To help us help you, include
sup.inc.1: Your phone model and Android version (Settings → About phone).

test.title: Be a tester - Big Cube Solver
test.h1: Test Big Cube Solver before anyone else
test.intro: The app solves any cube from 2×2 to 15×15. Before it goes on Google Play it needs testers. Three steps on your Android phone (5.0 or newer), with the same Google account you use in the Play Store.
test.s1.d: Open the group and tap Join group. Nobody else sees your email.
test.s2.d: Tap Become a tester. If it says it is not available, wait a few minutes after step 1 and try again.
test.s3.d: From Google Play, like any app. Updates arrive by themselves.
test.ask: One important favour: keep the app installed for at least 14 days and open it now and then. Google requires 12 testers for 14 days in a row before it allows publishing.
test.tell.d: Everything helps: what you liked, what failed, what was unclear. It takes two minutes.
test.q1.d: The phone uses a different Google account than the one that joined the group. In the Play Store tap your picture, switch to that account and repeat step 3.
test.q2.d: For now the app is Android only.
test.q3.h: Is it free? Does it collect data?
test.q3.d: The test version is free. The app has no ads or accounts and sends nothing over the internet: privacy policy.
guide.title: What to try - Big Cube Solver
guide.intro: No need to try everything. What helps most: use the app as you really would, and tell us what happened.
guide.1.d: Pick a size (the size button), tap the dice to scramble and the wand to solve. Try a big one: 10×10 or 15×15. In the test every size is unlocked.
guide.2.d: Tap the camera and show each face. Works best in good light without glare. Tell us your cube size and whether it read the colours right.
guide.3.h: Follow the solution with the cube in your hands
guide.3.d: Step move by move, change the speed, go back. Is every turn clear? Did your cube end up solved?
guide.4.d: Menu → Patterns: form one on your cube. In My patterns save the cube on screen and share it as a link with another tester.
guide.5.h: If you have one: a picture cube or a smart cube
guide.5.d: Picture cube: photograph it solved, then scrambled. Bluetooth smart cube: connect it and follow a guided solution.
guide.6.d: Turn the cube on screen with your finger until it is solved... and see what happens.
guide.wrong.2: If the app closes by itself, it shows a report the next time it opens: share it.
guide.wrong.3: Tell us your phone model, what you did and what you expected.

com.title: Community - Big Cube Solver
com.intro: Our Discord server is where players and the Big Cube Solver team meet: ask for help, report a problem, suggest what to build next and share what you solve.
com.free: Free. You need a Discord account; you do not need the app to join.
com.ch.help: #help-en and #ayuda-es - questions about the app, answered in English and Spanish.
com.ch.bugs: #bug-reports - something went wrong? Tell us your phone model, Android version and app version, and add a screenshot if you can.
com.ch.ideas: #ideas - suggest features and vote for the ones you want with reactions.
com.ch.pat: #patterns - share pattern links; they open straight in the app.
com.ch.smart: #smart-cubes - GAN, Giiker, QiYi, GoCube and Rubik's Connected.
com.ch.skins: #skins - share sticker sheets that turn the cube on screen into a picture cube.
com.rules: Be kind, stay on topic, no spam. Discord's own terms and privacy policy apply on the server; this site and the app still collect nothing.
com.email: Prefer email? Support answers at support@bigcubesolver.com.
home.comm.d: Get help, share patterns and skins, and tell us what to build next - on the Big Cube Solver Discord server.
